title: Gold Has Risen Fivefold in a Decade; Motilal Oswal Sees Rs 1.68 Lakh Ahead
excerpt: Motilal Oswal's quarterly bullion report expects domestic gold at Rs 1.60-1.68 lakh per 10 grams within 6 to 12 months, against about Rs 30,000 at Diwali 2016 and around Rs 1.5 lakh this Dhanteras.
body:
• Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) expects domestic gold to reach Rs 1.60 lakh to Rs 1.68 lakh per 10 grams over the next 6 to 12 months, according to its latest quarterly bullion report — a forecast, not a result.
  • The same report puts international gold at $4,500 to $4,700 an ounce in the medium term, and domestic prices around Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 grams in the short term.
  • Gold was about Rs 30,000 per 10 grams around Diwali 2016 and is around Rs 1.5 lakh at Diwali 2026 — roughly a fivefold rise in a decade, the report notes.
  • For buyers today, Dhanteras: the brokerage's guidance, as reported, is to accumulate on dips rather than chase the peak — the Rs 1.68 lakh figure is a 6-to-12-month target, not a promise about this week's price.

Gold has become five times more expensive in a decade, and one of India's largest brokerages expects the climb to continue. In its latest quarterly bullion report, Motilal Oswal Financial Services estimates that domestic gold could reach Rs 1.60 lakh to Rs 1.68 lakh per 10 grams in the next 6 to 12 months, Aaj Tak reported. The report expects international gold to reach $4,500 to $4,700 an ounce in the medium term, with domestic prices around Rs 1.48 lakh per 10 grams in the short term.

A decade measured in diyas

The Diwali-to-Diwali comparison in the report is stark. Around Diwali 2016, gold was about Rs 30,000 per 10 grams. By Diwali 2026 it is around Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams — a fivefold increase over ten festival seasons, according to the report's figures as summarised by Tezzbuzz. Families buying gold today, on Dhanteras, are paying in one purchase what five equivalent purchases cost a decade ago.

Why the brokerage stays bullish

Navneet Damani, head of commodity research at MOFSL, said gold continues to retain its importance as a safe investment amid global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, according to the report's summary. The brokerage's strategy guidance, as reported, is to buy on dips rather than time the peak: it identifies spot gold between $3,800 and $3,900 an ounce as an accumulation zone on the global market, with a short-term target of $4,200 before the medium-term range. Those are the brokerage's estimates, and the report itself notes actual prices may move with global conditions.

What to watch

Two cautions belong next to the headline number. First, a forecast range is not a price: the same report puts the short-term domestic level below today's, at around Rs 1.48 lakh, which implies the path to Rs 1.68 lakh is not expected to be straight. Second, gold at around Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams is already at levels that have changed buying behaviour — the metal's decade-long run means the jewellery-versus-investment decision Indian families make every Dhanteras now involves sums five times larger than in 2016. The next checkpoints are the international price against the report's $4,500-$4,700 medium-term range and whether domestic prices hold the report's short-term level.
